**🔥 THE BIG STORY**

The king is gone. Jensen Huang, the founder, CEO, and leather-jacketed icon who steered Nvidia for 33 years to become the undisputed engine of the AI revolution, has resigned. His ouster follows an investigation into an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset, a scandal with national security implications. This isn't just a leadership change; it's a seismic shock to the entire AI ecosystem, which has been built almost entirely on the back of Nvidia's hardware and Huang's singular, aggressive vision. The immediate implication most will miss: the sudden power vacuum at Nvidia introduces a new, massive variable of instability into the AI arms race, forcing every player to question their deep-seated dependency on a single supplier and dramatically accelerating the search for alternatives. [S8][S9][S10][S17][S25][S31][S99]

---

**🛠️ TOOL DROPS & UPDATES**

-   **Google launches Gemini Decisions API.**
    This new API is built for "fast, calibrated multimodal decisions," moving beyond simple classification to provide outputs with confidence scores. Who cares: This is for anyone building systems that need to make high-stakes choices (e.g., fraud detection, medical imaging analysis, A/B test selection) and need to know *how sure* the model is. [S130][S139]

-   **Runway ships Praxis-1, an open-weight robotics model.**
    The video AI company has released a "world action model" for robotics, available with open weights for developers to build on with partners like Noble Machines and Standard Bots. Who cares: This is a major move to generalize robotic actions, potentially doing for physical automation what LLMs did for text. [S41]

-   **Amazon unveils Ring Robotics for autonomous security.**
    The new lineup includes an autonomous drone and a rover designed to patrol businesses and properties, extending the Ring surveillance network into mobile platforms. Who cares: This is a significant step toward automated physical security, merging Amazon's consumer hardware dominance with its AI and robotics ambitions. [S51][S107][S108]

-   **Phota Labs automates professional photo editing.**
    A new service uses AI to automatically turn everyday photos into professional-looking shots, aiming to replace complex editing software with a one-click process. Who cares: For anyone who takes photos but isn't a professional editor, this promises pro results without the learning curve. [S6]

-   **ChatGPT gets business profile features.**
    A new guide explains how businesses can claim and set up their official presence on ChatGPT, suggesting a push toward making the platform a more direct interface between companies and customers. Who cares: This positions ChatGPT as a new kind of business directory or "yellow pages," where discovery and interaction happen via chat. [S62]

---

**🎯 USE CASE SPOTLIGHT — BY ROLE**

-   **📣 Product Marketer**
    Use Adobe's new CX Enterprise Coworker to automate content creation for different channels, ensuring brand consistency across your supply chain. [S28] Also, deploy AI agents to analyze your Amazon ad campaign data, cutting down the time it takes to get actionable insights from weeks to hours. [S63]

-   **📋 Product Manager**
    Prototype a feature prioritization system using the new Gemini Decisions API; feed it multimodal user feedback (e.g., screen recordings + text reviews) to get a "calibrated" score on which feature to build next. [S130]

-   **🎨 Designer (UI/UX)**
    Use the new `expo/exact` framework to have an AI agent build, run, and visually test your app's UI across web, macOS, iOS, and Linux, drastically speeding up cross-platform consistency checks. [S137]

-   **📸 Photographer**
    Upload a batch of event photos to Phota Labs to automate the culling and editing process, turning a multi-hour job into a few minutes and delivering polished shots to clients faster. [S6]

-   **🎬 Videographer & Filmmaker**
    Today’s data offers no new specific tools or use cases for this role.

-   **📱 App Developer**
    Integrate the new Gemini Decisions API to build features that require reliable, high-speed decision-making with confidence scores, like in-app content moderation or dynamic UI adjustments. [S130] For Android devs, experiment with the `Mika` repo to build an on-device agent that can operate other apps to complete tasks for the user. [S134]

---

**🔬 FROM THE LABS**

**RAG systems fail spectacularly under pressure.**
A new study reveals that the accuracy of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems plummets as the amount of "distracting" information grows. What they built: A reproducible test that measured RAG performance against a knowledge base that expanded to 2.68 million passages. What it beat: It didn't beat anything; it broke the assumption that RAG scales gracefully. Accuracy dropped by 40 percentage points as the context window filled with irrelevant documents. Why it matters: This is a massive red flag for enterprises building chatbots and search tools over huge internal document sets. It proves that simply stuffing more data into a vector database isn't a viable strategy; in 6-12 months, the most valuable products will be those that master sophisticated filtering and re-ranking *before* feeding context to a model. [S11]

---

**🚚 AI IN LOGISTICS & SUPPLY CHAIN**

-   **GXO targets 1,000 humanoid robots for its warehouses.**
    The logistics giant plans a massive deployment of Apollo humanoids if current trials prove successful, signaling a major bet on general-purpose robots for warehouse tasks. This move validates the humanoid form factor for logistics and puts pressure on competitors to develop their own automation strategies beyond fixed AMRs. [S42]

-   **Fura Freight’s AI agent is already booking 40% of its loads.**
    The freight brokerage's AI agent, "Donna," is automating a huge chunk of its core business, with a goal to hit 90% next year. This is a real-world proof point that AI agents can move beyond chat and handle complex, revenue-generating workflows in freight logistics. [S120][S121]

-   **Humble Robotics raises $51M for autonomous and electric freight.**
    The Series A funding will help the company scale its unified approach to autonomous trucking. This investment signals continued confidence that long-haul trucking is ripe for automation, despite economic headwinds. [S87]

-   **Runway launches a foundational model for robotics.**
    The release of Praxis-1 with open weights provides a new software layer for robotics companies to build upon, potentially accelerating the development of more capable and general-purpose robots for warehouses and last-mile delivery. [S41]

-   **Amazon gets green light for UK drone expansion; faces noise complaints in US.**
    While Amazon received UK approval to expand its Prime Air delivery service, US residents are lodging complaints about the "constant buzz" from drones. This highlights the dual challenge of regulation and public acceptance as last-mile drone delivery scales. [S66][S78][S82]

-   **Cainiao unveils a new, more efficient warehouse climbing robot.**
    Alibaba's logistics arm introduced an upgraded robot capable of four-side retrieval and enabling denser storage. This is another step in specialized warehouse automation, focusing on maximizing cubic space utilization—a key metric for e-commerce fulfillment. [S93]

---

**💸 MONEY & MOVES**

-   **Fractile raises a staggering $720M for AI chips.**
    The British startup's massive funding round makes it a top-funded player in the race to build purpose-built AI processors. This signals a major European bet on challenging Nvidia's dominance, a sentiment likely to intensify with Nvidia's leadership crisis. [S122]

-   **Norwest launches a $4B fund with a deep focus on AI.**
    The venture firm's largest fund to date is a clear sign that, despite market turbulence, top-tier investors are doubling down on AI as the primary driver of future growth. [S19]

-   **Humble Robotics lands $51M for autonomous freight.**
    The Series A round will scale the company's work in autonomous and electric trucking. Money is flowing into startups that are automating physical-world industries like logistics. [S87]

-   **SoftBank posts a $3B loss on a failed AI energy bet.**
    The investment giant lost billions pre-ordering natural gas turbines to power future AI data centers. This is a cautionary tale about the immense, and often misjudged, energy requirements underpinning the AI boom. [S5]

---

**🤖 OPEN SOURCE WATCH**

-   **agentes-chat/agentes-chat**
    It's a self-hosted, open-source Slack alternative where human teams and AI agents collaborate in channels. Created 3 days ago, it's rocketing up at ~337 stars/day. For teams looking to build agentic workflows without being locked into a proprietary platform. [S136]

-   **KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop**
    This tool lets you run a command-line agent in the background that works autonomously and only surfaces decisions for human approval when it's unsure. Created 9 days ago, it has a velocity of ~526 stars/day. Try this if you're exploring ways to give agents more autonomy without losing control. [S135]

-   **wangzan101/Mika**
    An on-device AI agent for Android that can operate other apps and navigate the web to execute tasks. Launched about two weeks ago, it's gaining ~598 stars/day. This is for mobile developers experimenting with the next generation of proactive, OS-level assistants. [S134]

---

**🗣️ HACKER NEWS PULSE**

-   **Gemini Decisions API**
    The thread vibe is cautiously optimistic, with developers trying to parse what "calibrated multimodal decisions" truly means. The sharpest take: "If Google has genuinely solved calibrated probabilities for production use, this is a game-changer for any industry where 'how confident are you?' is more important than 'what is it?'—think finance, medicine, and safety-critical systems." [S139]

-   **Lock Your GitHub Actions**
    The comment section is a mix of security best practices and war stories about CI/CD pipeline vulnerabilities. The sharpest take: "Pinning action versions is basic hygiene, but it's security theater if you don't vet the supply chain of the action itself. You're just locking in a dependency on an upstream project that could be compromised at any time." [S140]

-   **Swatters are using AI voices to deceive 911 dispatchers**
    The discussion is grim, focusing on the inevitable misuse of powerful, easily accessible AI tools like voice cloning. The sharpest take: "This was completely predictable. The defense against this won't be technological; it will have to be procedural. Every system that relies on voice-for-trust is now officially broken." [S145]

---

**⚡ SPEED ROUND**

-   Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before the U.S. Congress. [S8]
-   President Trump suggested on Truth Social that Apple's Tim Cook should replace Huang at Nvidia. [S14]
-   A cyberattack on service provider Fireworks AI allowed hackers to access Notion customers' chat transcripts. [S22]
-   SoftBank lost over $3 billion betting that natural gas turbines would be the best way to power future AI data centers. [S5]
-   Meta’s longtime head of infrastructure, Santosh Janardhan, is stepping down. [S111]
-   Adobe has officially introduced an agentic AI "Coworker" to help automate content supply chains. [S28]
-   Logistics giant GXO is planning to deploy up to 1,000 Apollo humanoid robots in its warehouses pending successful trials. [S42]
-   Tractor Supply is now partnering with Uber to offer same-day on-demand delivery. [S12]
-   Autonomous trucks are projected to be cheaper to operate than human-driven ones in the U.S. by 2028. [S68]
-   Hugging Face's CEO reaffirmed his commitment to open-source AI following the turmoil at Nvidia. [S1]

---

**🎮 TODAY'S DAILY CHALLENGE — TRY THIS IN 15 MINUTES**

Today's most interesting new capability is Google's Gemini Decisions API, which promises to go beyond classification to make "calibrated decisions."

-   **The tool to use:** Google AI Studio (aistudio.google.com). The Decisions API is available there for free.
-   **The exact workflow to try:**
    1.  Find three different images of a product concept (e.g., three different sneaker designs, three different website mockups).
    2.  In AI Studio, use a multimodal prompt with the Gemini Decision model.
    3.  Upload your three images and use a prompt like this:
        `"Analyze these three website landing page designs. Based on modern UI/UX principles for maximizing user conversion, which of these three designs is the best choice to deploy for an A/B test? Provide a calibrated decision with confidence scores for each option and a brief rationale."`
-   **What I'm testing for:** Look at the output format. Does it give you a clear "winner"? More importantly, look at the confidence scores. Are they "calibrated" — meaning, does a 90% confidence score feel meaningfully different from a 70% one? How does this feel different from just asking a standard model to "pick the best one"?
-   **Why this matters right now:** AI is moving from being a generator of options to a decider between them. An API that can make a reliable, explainable choice with a confidence level is a building block for automating countless business processes that currently require human judgment. [S130][S139][S144]

---

**🧠 EDGE INSIGHT**

The ouster of Jensen Huang doesn't just destabilize Nvidia; it ends the "lazy" era of AI infrastructure strategy. For the last five years, the default answer for anyone building AI has been "buy more Nvidia GPUs." It was easy, correct, and required no strategic thought. That certainty is now gone. The second-order effect is that every CTO and head of engineering is being forced to become a supply chain and geopolitics expert overnight. In the next 90 days, we'll see a frantic acceleration of "Plan B" hardware strategies — not as experiments, but as mission-critical de-risking. This means more serious investment in rival chipmakers (like the freshly funded Fractile), a genuine push for custom silicon (TPUs, Trainium, etc.), and a new premium on software layers (like Viam for robotics) that abstract away hardware dependency. The fall of the king forces every vassal to build their own castle.
